7c7d9ea7598db01e4e5b475b26d01c94ad6bf03a: Brunico – Kronplatz offers 125 km of well-marked runs: a mid-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 32 lifts are generally sufficient to handle capacity in peak season. Its reputation as a family resort is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. The altitude of Brunico – Kronplatz (838 m at the bottom, 2275 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover through mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay at Brunico – Kronplatz is clearly high: 80€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Brunico – Kronplatz lives up to its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most types of skier without disappointing.
7c84c320d07a2dfbbb58b4aa534af8d4df12a411: Two large ski areas, but two radically different ways of spending a ski holiday. Val d'Isère is the sporting and prestige reference of the Tarentaise. 7c90dce39b5a3c021cb510461f98df91a7851d25: The Baqueira Beret ski area, with its 173 km of pistes, offers a fine range for every type of skier: large enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. The 36 lifts let you link descents without long queues. Baqueira Beret's DNA is high-end: the accommodation, mountain restaurants and resort services reflect a clientele that doesn't count the cost. With a day lift pass at 72€, the stay has a price, but the experience lives up to it for those who want to indulge without compromise. With a summit at 2,610 m and a village at 1,500 m, Baqueira Beret's snow cover is generally reliable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but conditions recover quickly once serious snowfalls arrive. The budget for a stay at Baqueira Beret is clearly high: 72€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before setting off. In short: Baqueira Beret isn't for everyone, but for those who can afford it, it is probably one of the best skiing experiences in Europe.

7cce049c8b772404d3b4944be1de35ac93b00ec7: Kellerjoch is a little-known resort on a modest scale – 14 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Kellerjoch's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for learning to ski with children. Kellerjoch's modest altitude – base at 1352 m, summit at 1887 m – makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the most reliable months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking snow reports before you leave is strongly advised. The day lift pass at 46€ places Kellerjoch among the intermediate resorts in terms of budget – neither a bargain nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Kellerjoch doesn't rival the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
